report.source_text: Rheumatology, on the other hand, recommended prednisone therapy at a dose of 1 mg/kg (equivalent to 80 mg daily) as treatment for vasculitis. Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole was also administered while the patient was on high-dose steroids. Additionally, methotrexate (MTX) was introduced, with a weekly oral dose of 20 mg, along with daily folic acid supplementation to mitigate potential side effects.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 26-year-old Hispanic female with a history of recurrent severe chest pain since age 17, initially associated with heartburn and responsive to antacids, presented with increased frequency of episodes. Laboratory tests on admission showed significant systemic inflammation with elevated WBC (12.8 × 10^9/L), CRP (1.3 mg/dL), and ESR (79 mm/hour). Imaging with CT angiography revealed extensive wall thickening and mild narrowing of the descending thoracic and suprarenal abdominal aorta. PET CT demonstrated active metabolic vasculitis in the aorta and major peripheral arteries including subclavian and iliofemoral arteries. Despite absence of reported physical exam signs (pulse asymmetry, bruits) or systemic symptoms documentation (fever, weight loss, claudication), rheumatology initiated immunosuppressive therapy with high-dose prednisone and methotrexate, reflecting clinical confidence in the diagnosis.
